notes: The pi-stop plugs directly onto four adjacent header pins (no breadboard or jumper wires), as shown in the image: R->GPIO22, A->GPIO27, G->GPIO17, GND->GND next to GPIO17.
The manual says 'or 3x LEDs and resistors' as an alternative, but gives no wiring for it, so the pi-stop build is used.
Which GND header pin is used is not labelled in the image; GND.1 is used as a representative (all Pi GND pins are symmetric).
Pi-stop is a new part type; its ports are modelled as header-sockets and R/A/G each conduct through an LED to the common GND.
The Pi's power, USB and software (Mu, gpiozero) are not modelled as parts.
